Classic Yule Log (Bûche de Noël)

Served at: Christmas Day

Serves 8-10Prep 45 minCook 12 min

The Yule Log, or Bûche de Noël, is a traditional French dessert served during Christmas. It's a festive chocolate sponge cake rolled with a creamy filling, then decorated to resemble a rustic log, symbolizing the ancient custom of burning a Yule log to bring good fortune in the new year. This elegant dessert is a beautiful and delicious centerpiece for your Christmas Day celebration.

Ingredients

  • 4 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 cup (60g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 cup (25g) unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 cup (226g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 3 cups (360g) powdered sugar, sifted
  • 1/2 cup (50g) unsweetened cocoa powder, sifted
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) milk or heavy cream
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Pinch of salt
  • 2 tablespoons powdered sugar, for dusting
  • Fresh cranberries, for decoration
  • Fresh rosemary sprigs, for decoration

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a 10x15 inch (25x38 cm) jelly roll pan with parchment paper, extending it over the short sides for easy lifting. Lightly grease the parchment.
  2. In a large bowl, beat the eggs and 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar with an electric mixer on high speed for 5-7 minutes, until light, thick, and pale yellow, forming ribbons when the beaters are lifted.
  3. In a separate small bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup (25g) unsweetened cocoa powder, baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
  4. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture in two additions, being careful not to deflate the batter. Fold in 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
  5. Spread the batter evenly into the prepared jelly roll pan. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the cake springs back when lightly touched.
  6. While the cake bakes, lay a clean kitchen towel on a flat surface and generously dust it with powdered sugar.
  7. Immediately invert the hot cake onto the sugared towel. Carefully peel off the parchment paper. Trim off any crisp edges of the cake.
  8. Starting from a short end, carefully roll the cake and the towel together into a tight log. Let it cool completely, seam-side down, on a wire rack (about 30-45 minutes).
  9. While the cake cools, prepare the chocolate buttercream: In a large bowl, beat the softened unsalted butter with an electric mixer until creamy.
  10. Gradually add the 3 cups (360g) sifted powdered sugar and 1/2 cup (50g) sifted cocoa powder, beating until combined. Add 1/4 cup (60ml) milk or heavy cream, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt. Beat on high speed until light and fluffy, about 3-5 minutes.
  11. Once the cake is completely cool, carefully unroll it. Spread about 1/2 to 3/4 cup of the chocolate buttercream evenly over the inside surface of the cake.
  12. Carefully re-roll the cake tightly, without the towel. Place the log seam-side down on a serving platter.
  13. Using a serrated knife, slice off a small piece from one end of the log at an angle. Position this piece on the side of the main log to resemble a cut-off branch.
  14. Frost the entire cake log and the 'branch' with the remaining chocolate buttercream. Use a fork to create a bark-like texture all over the frosting.
  15. Dust the Yule Log generously with 2 tablespoons powdered sugar to resemble snow. Arrange fresh cranberries and rosemary sprigs around and on top of the log for decoration.
  16. Refrigerate the Yule Log for at least 1 hour before serving to allow the frosting to set and flavors to meld. Remove from the refrigerator 15-20 minutes before serving for optimal texture.

Tips

  • For an extra rich flavor, you can brush the unrolled cake with a tablespoon or two of coffee liqueur or rum before spreading the buttercream.
  • To make meringue mushrooms for decoration, beat 2 egg whites with 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar until soft peaks form, then gradually add 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla, beating until stiff and glossy. Pipe caps and stems onto parchment-lined baking sheets and bake at 200°F (95°C) for 1-2 hours until dry. 'Glue' them together with a dab of buttercream and dust with cocoa powder.
  • The Yule Log can be assembled and refrigerated up to 2 days in advance. Add the powdered sugar, cranberries, and rosemary just before serving for the freshest look.
